name: hook_iat_ac
description: Cross-process IAT hook against AssaultCube (32-bit ac_client.exe). Attacker locates the IAT slot for user32.dll!GetAsyncKeyState (called every frame by AC's input loop) and overwrites it with a trampoline shellcode address. Same primitive as hook_iat against TestTarget — this variant validates the fingerprint against a real game process and a real per-frame input import. GetAsyncKeyState is chosen because it is (a) imported by ac_client.exe, (b) called every frame at high rate (>60 Hz) so the trampoline counter reliably reads nonzero within the verify window, and (c) a documented target for aim-assist and trigger-bot cheats that need to detect key presses ahead of the game loop. Alternative imports for future runs: user32.dll!GetCursorPos (mouse position), kernel32.dll!Sleep (frame pacing).

extra.target_selection_notes: kernel32.dll!Sleep is used by SDL 1.2 for frame pacing and is imported by ac_client.exe. Original attempt targeted user32.dll!GetAsyncKeyState but AC uses the Win32 message loop (PeekMessageA + WM_KEYDOWN) for input rather than polling GetAsyncKeyState, so that import isn't present. --verify-hits 0 skips the runtime-firing counter check because AC's Sleep call cadence depends on frame rate — install-only verification suffices for the fingerprint capture. Use `ProcessToolkit.exe list-imports --pid <ac_pid>` to enumerate ac_client's actual imports when picking new targets.
extra.expected_fingerprint: PE header walk + import descriptor walk yields 6-12 small READVM_REMOTE events; 1x ALLOCVM_REMOTE (~4KB RWX); 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (trampoline write, ~4KB); 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (IAT page RO->RW); 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (4-byte slot overwrite); 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (restore). Small WRITEVM lands in ac_client.exe's IAT (parsable via pe_utils), NOT in .text — this is the distinguishing signal vs hook_inline_ac.
